title: A finitely presented factor algebra with standard smooth reduction
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subset R$ an ideal, and $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra. Suppose $\Lambda/I\Lambda$ is a filtered colimit [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras] of standard smooth $R/I$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. For every finitely presented $R$-algebra $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and $R$-algebra map $\varphi:A\to\Lambda$, there exist a finitely presented $R$-algebra $A\prime$ and $R$-algebra maps $\iota:A\to A\prime$ and $\varphi\prime:A\prime\to\Lambda$ with $\varphi\prime\circ\iota=\varphi$ such that $A\prime/IA\prime$ is standard smooth over $R/I$. No nilpotence hypothesis is imposed on $I$.

proof.text: Obtain finite polynomial data g and variable lifts from the standard smooth stage of the reduced map. Each evaluated relation lies in ILambda; its reduced polynomial quotient B is standard smooth.

Use Ideal.map = span(image I) and Finsupp.mem_ideal_span_range_iff_exists_finsupp to write every evaluated relation as a finite sum of epsilon_ij*mu_ij, with epsilon_ij in I. Reindex each finite support by Fin(N_i); the private helper exists_sum_of_mem_map proves this step.

Define variables Fin(n) + ULift(Sigma i, Fin(N_i)), corrected polynomials g_i - sum epsilon_ij*delta_ij, their generated ideal J, and A prime as the actual quotient. Evaluate old variables at the chosen lifts and correction variables at mu. The finite-sum identities make every corrected relation vanish. Ideal.span_le and Ideal.Quotient.lift_a give phi prime. On coefficients its composite with the canonical A -> A prime is phi. All these constructions and equalities are proved in the item.

The polynomial algebra over A is finitely presented over R, and J is finitely generated by a finite range. Apply Algebra.FinitePresentation.quotient. The ULift on the correction-variable set gives the exact max(u,v,w) carrier universe without transporting the ring.

Apply the explicit reduction isomorphism Q/IQ = B[delta]. The already proved source-library instance MvPolynomial.isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension gives standard smoothness of the polynomial extension over B. Compose with standard smoothness of B using IsStandardSmooth.trans and transport along the inverse isomorphism using IsStandardSmooth.of_algEquiv.
